subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only or self-deny tool policy that hides selected tools from the requester while preserving them for spawned subagents, and what public config/API shape should define that boundary?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but the fix changes a security-sensitive authorization model and adds public config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent semantics.

options.title: Add delegate-only config
options.body: Define a `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly`-style field with absolute deny precedence, audit visibility, docs, and tests for requester, child, ACP, and unsupported-runtime behavior.

options.title: Fold into spawn-policy design
options.body: Keep this open until the per-spawn tool-policy work also covers requester-hidden but child-inherited tools without creating a second competing contract.

options.title: Reject core surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or prompt-level delegation as the supported pattern, accepting that config-enforced separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Add delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Define a `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly`-style field with absolute deny precedence, audit visibility, docs, and tests for requester, child, ACP, and unsupported-runtime behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent area and maintainer-routing signal for the cross-cutting tool-policy security decision.
